table.name: active_agency
table.remarks: One row per prison that has ever been switched on for managing property in DPS rather than NOMIS. The list is published on the public actuator /info payload, which is how the front end decides whether to offer the service at a prison. Switching a prison off flips the flag rather than deleting the row, so deactivation stays auditable and the toggle is idempotent.

column.name: agency_id
column.remarks: Primary key. Agency (prison) code. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: active
column.remarks: Whether the prison is currently switched on. False means it was switched on at some point and has since been switched off. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: updated_at
column.remarks: When the prison was last switched on or off. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: updated_by
column.remarks: DPS username of the member of staff who last changed the switch. Identifies a member of staff. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

table.name: legacy_cleanup_item
table.remarks: One container a legacy clean-up job intends to close, snapshotted with the action decided at request time. Processed one per transaction; the status records what happened to it.

column.name: id
column.remarks: Primary key. Time-ordered UUID v7. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: legacy_cleanup_job_id
column.remarks: The job this item belongs to. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: property_container_id
column.remarks: The container to close. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: prisoner_number
column.remarks: The prisoner number the container belonged to when the job was requested, so the item can be re-checked against prisoner-search without loading the container. Identifies a prisoner. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

column.name: action
column.remarks: RETURN (the person was released: mark returned) or TRANSFER (the person is at another prison: mark transferred there). [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: planned_event_date
column.remarks: The date the closing event will be dated to: the release date, or the date the person left this prison. Taken from prisoner-search when the job was requested. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

column.name: planned_to_prison_id
column.remarks: For TRANSFER, the prison the person is now at, which becomes the destination on the TRANSFERRED event. Null for RETURN. Locates a prisoner. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

column.name: status
column.remarks: PENDING, PROCESSED (the container was closed), SKIPPED (already removed, or no longer qualified on re-check) or FAILED (an error; the container is unchanged). [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: message
column.remarks: Why the item was skipped or failed, or a note that the domain event could not be published after the change was committed. Null when processed cleanly. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: processed_at
column.remarks: When the item reached its final status. Null while PENDING. [Sensitivity: NONE]

table.name: legacy_cleanup_job
table.remarks: One admin-requested run of the legacy property clean-up for a prison: closes containers still held there for people released or transferred out before a cut-off date, marking each RETURNED or TRANSFERRED. Processed asynchronously from an SQS work queue, one container per transaction; the counters are updated as it goes so progress can be watched.

column.name: id
column.remarks: Primary key. Time-ordered UUID v7. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: prison_id
column.remarks: The prison whose held property is being cleaned up. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: status
column.remarks: PENDING (requested, not yet claimed by a listener), STARTED (being processed) or FINISHED. A partial unique index allows one PENDING or STARTED job per prison. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: older_than_days
column.remarks: The look-back window the admin chose: only people who left at least this many days before the request are in scope. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: cutoff_date
column.remarks: The request date minus older_than_days; a person must have left on or before this date to be in scope. Stored so the rule the job applied is reproducible. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: requested_by
column.remarks: DPS username of the admin who requested the run. The property events the run writes are attributed to the LEGACY_CLEANUP system user, so this is the only record of who asked for them. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: requested_at
column.remarks: When the run was requested. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: start_time
column.remarks: When a listener first claimed the job and began processing. Null while PENDING. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: last_activity_at
column.remarks: When the job last made progress. A STARTED job with no activity for 30 minutes is treated as abandoned (its pod died) and may be re-claimed by a redelivered message; only unprocessed items are then resumed. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: end_time
column.remarks: When processing finished. Null until FINISHED. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: total_records
column.remarks: How many containers were snapshotted as items when the job was requested. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: returned_records
column.remarks: How many items have been marked RETURNED so far. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: transferred_records
column.remarks: How many items have been marked TRANSFERRED so far. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: skipped_records
column.remarks: How many items were skipped: the container had already been removed by staff, or the person no longer qualified when re-checked against prisoner-search at processing time. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: failed_records
column.remarks: How many items failed with an error; the container was left unchanged and the message on the item says why. [Sensitivity: NONE]

table.name: property_container
table.remarks: A sealed container of one prisoner's property. The record is event-sourced: its history lives in property_event and its current status and location are derived from the most recent relevant event. Five values are mirrored into columns here (seal number, status, internal location, storage location type, receiving prison) so the establishment-wide list can filter and page in SQL; the derivation stays authoritative and every write refreshes the mirrors.

column.name: id
column.remarks: Primary key. Time-ordered UUID v7, so insert order matches id order. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: prisoner_number
column.remarks: NOMIS offender number (noms id) of the prisoner whose property this is. The link that makes every row here personal data about that prisoner. Reassigned when NOMIS merges two prisoner numbers for the same person: the containers move to the surviving number and the retired one survives only as removedNomsNumber on the resulting domain event. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

column.name: prison_id
column.remarks: Agency (prison) code holding the container. Read with prisoner_number it indicates where that prisoner's property is, and normally where the prisoner is. Not reassigned on a transfer out - the receiving prison creates its own record. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

column.name: container_type
column.remarks: What kind of property the container holds. One of STANDARD, EXCESS, VALUABLES, CONFISCATED. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: create_datetime
column.remarks: When the container record was created in this service. For containers migrated from NOMIS this is the migration run, not the original prison event. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: created_by_user_id
column.remarks: DPS username of the member of staff who created the container. Identifies a member of staff. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: proposed_disposal_date
column.remarks: Date the container is proposed for disposal. Disposal status is derived by comparing this with today rather than being stored, so a container becomes DISPOSAL_REQUIRED without anything writing to it. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: current_seal_number
column.remarks: Seal number currently on the container. Stored rather than derived because uniqueness across containers in storage is checked in SQL. Freed for re-use once the container leaves active storage. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: removal_outcome
column.remarks: Why the container left active storage: DISPOSED, RETURNED, TRANSFERRED, COMBINED, CREATED_IN_ERROR or REMOVED. Null while the container is in active storage. All are terminal except REMOVED, which a REACTIVATED event reverses - which is why there is no archived flag. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: removal_date
column.remarks: Date the container left active storage. Null while it is still held. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: current_status
column.remarks: Denormalised mirror of the derived status, excluding the time-based disposal overlay so the column stays stable over time. One of STORED, DUE_FOR_TRANSFER_OUT, DUE_FOR_RETURN, DISPOSAL_REQUIRED, DISPOSED, RETURNED, TRANSFER, COMBINED, CREATED_IN_ERROR, REMOVED. Read the events, not this column, if you need the authoritative status. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: current_internal_location_id
column.remarks: Denormalised mirror of the container's current storage location - a location UUID in hmpps-locations-inside-prison-api. Null when the container is offsite at Branston, has no recorded location, or has left active storage. This is where the property is kept, not where the prisoner is. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: current_storage_location_type
column.remarks: Denormalised mirror of where the container is stored: INTERNAL (a location within the prison) or BRANSTON (the offsite warehouse, which has no internal location id). [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: receiving_prison_id
column.remarks: Agency code of the prison this container is due to be transferred in to, denormalised so the establishment list can surface incoming property. Set only while the container is due for transfer out, or transferred but not yet reconciled with the receiving prison's record. Indicates where the owning prisoner has moved to. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

table.name: property_event
table.remarks: One thing that happened to a container, in an ordered history. This is the authoritative record: the container's current seal, status and location are derived from the most recent relevant event, and the columns on property_container are mirrors of that derivation. Events are appended, never amended, so this table is also the audit trail.

column.name: id
column.remarks: Primary key. Time-ordered UUID v7. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: property_container_id
column.remarks: Foreign key to property_container - the container this event happened to. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: event_type
column.remarks: What happened. One of CREATED_SEALED, SEAL_CHANGED, CONTAINER_TYPE_CHANGE, MOVED, TRANSFERRED, RETURNED, DISPOSAL_REQUIRED, DISPOSED, COMBINED, CREATED_IN_ERROR, REMOVED, REACTIVATED, or the four driven by prisoner movements - PRISONER_TRANSFERRED_OUT, PRISONER_RECEIVED, PRISONER_RELEASED, DIED_IN_CUSTODY. Each type implies a status. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: seal_number
column.remarks: Seal number recorded by this event, on the event types that carry one (creation and reseal). Null on events that do not change the seal. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: event_datetime
column.remarks: When the event happened. Events are ordered by this; where two share a timestamp the later-appended one wins. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: from_internal_location_id
column.remarks: Storage location the container moved from - a location UUID in hmpps-locations-inside-prison-api. Null when the event does not move it. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: to_internal_location_id
column.remarks: Storage location the container moved to - a location UUID in hmpps-locations-inside-prison-api. Null when the event does not move it, or when it moved offsite to Branston (which has no internal location id). [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: from_prison_id
column.remarks: Agency code the container was held at before this event. Set on events that move it between prisons. Indicates the prisoner's previous establishment. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

column.name: to_prison_id
column.remarks: Agency code the container is going to. Set on a transfer out, and on the PRISONER_RECEIVED that flags property as due to follow its owner - so it indicates where the prisoner has moved to. [Sensitivity: PERSONAL]

column.name: event_user_id
column.remarks: DPS username of the member of staff who performed the action, or a reserved system user: PRISONER_PROPERTY_API for events raised by NOMIS sync or the prisoner movement listener, LEGACY_CLEANUP for closures written by a legacy clean-up job. Identifies a member of staff. [Sensitivity: STAFF]

column.name: event_date
column.remarks: The date the underlying prison activity happened, where it differs from when it was recorded (for example a disposal logged after the event). Null when the recorded timestamp is the date. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: to_storage_location_type
column.remarks: The kind of location the container moved to: INTERNAL or BRANSTON. Older events recorded an internal location id without an explicit type, and are read as INTERNAL. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: related_container_id
column.remarks: The other container involved: the one this container was combined into, or the matching record at the other end of a transfer. Filled in later on a transfer out, once the receiving prison logs the arrival and the two records are reconciled. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: container_type
column.remarks: The container's type at the moment of the event, snapshotted so the history is a self-contained record. On a type change this holds the new type. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: related_container_seal_number
column.remarks: The related container's seal number as at this event, snapshotted so the history names it by the seal it had at the time rather than any later reseal. [Sensitivity: NONE]

column.name: legacy_cleanup_job_id
column.remarks: Set on the RETURNED or TRANSFERRED event when the closure was written by a legacy clean-up job rather than by staff; null on every other event. A TRANSFERRED event carrying it records where the person went for the history, but is never treated as property awaiting arrival at that prison. [Sensitivity: NONE]
